title: Traffic Shaping & Rate Limiting
intro: Rate limiters protect downstream services against resource exhaustion, denial of service attacks, and runaway client loops by enforcing throughput quotas.
objectives: Compare Token Bucket, Leaky Bucket, Fixed Window, and Sliding Window algorithms.
Implement distributed atomic rate counters in Redis using Lua scripts.
Handle client backoff with standardized HTTP 429 headers (Retry-After).
body:
Rate limiting governs the frequency with which clients invoke operations on an API. It shields internal databases and worker queues from saturation and enforces monetized subscription tiers.

### Algorithms
- **Token Bucket**: Tokens are continuously added to a bucket of capacity $B$ at rate $R$ tokens/second. Each request consumes 1 token. Allows bursts up to bucket capacity while guaranteeing average rate $R$.
- **Leaky Bucket**: Requests queue into a bucket with fixed capacity and drain at a constant rate. Enforces completely smooth, un-bursty output traffic.
- **Fixed Window Counter**: Divides time into fixed intervals (e.g. 1 minute). Vulnerable to edge bursts (2x quota during the window boundary).
- **Sliding Window Log / Counter**: Smooths window boundaries by weighting request counts across previous and current time slices.
keyIdea: Rate limiters must fail closed or open gracefully under failure; Token Bucket balances burst tolerance with strict long-term rate ceilings.

concepts.title: Distributed Atomic Enforcement
concepts.body: In a multi-server setup, rate limiting state must be coordinated. Redis with atomic Lua scripts or Redis Cell (`CL.THROTTLE`) ensures race-free token acquisition without distributed locking.

concepts.title: Standard HTTP Feedback
concepts.body: When a limit is reached, respond with `HTTP 429 Too Many Requests` along with `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, and `Retry-After` headers.

examples: Stripe API rate limiting users by API key using Redis sliding window logs.
GitHub REST API returning remaining quota in response headers.

quiz.prompt: Which rate limiting algorithm natively permits short traffic bursts up to a fixed maximum while strictly capping long-term throughput?
quiz.explanation: Token Bucket allows bursts when tokens have accumulated up to the bucket capacity, while the refill rate enforces the long-term throughput ceiling.
